title: Homogeneous descent from generation of the irrelevant quotient
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1] with total-degree grading [def-sc-p1-standard]. Let N be an S-module, also a k-module with compatible scalar tower, with an internal additive direct sum decomposition N=⊕_{j∈ℤ} N_j satisfying S_t N_j⊆N_{t+j} for all natural t. Let n_i (i∈Fin r) be homogeneous elements whose images span N/(x_0,x_1)N over k, and put Q=span_S{n_i}. For every integer j and x∈N_j there exist q∈Q and a,b∈N_{j-1} such that x=q+x_0a+x_1b. No finite-generation assumption on N is required.

source.place: proof: graded Hilbert syzygy theorem; standard graded Nakayama argument expanded in lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-generation, not explicit in the blueprint

proof.text: The span Q is closed under every homogeneous component projection. For a generator n_i of degree d_i, expand s∈S into its finitely many total-degree components. Each component times n_i belongs to N_{t+d_i}, whose degree-e projection is itself or zero. Induction on span membership, allowing an arbitrary extra polynomial scalar, proves closure for all q∈Q.

proof.text: For every variable x_i, its multiplication shifts the degree projection by one: π_e(x_i y)=x_i π_{e-1}(y). Prove this for homogeneous y by direct-sum independence and the scalar grading compatibility, and extend to all y by finite additive decomposition.

proof.text: Induction on the k-span of the quotient generator images lifts a quotient linear expression to q∈Q; compatibility of k and S scalar actions handles the scalar step. Thus x-q∈(x_0,x_1)N. The range of the two variables is {x_0,x_1}; distribution of ideal multiplication over their two principal ideals expresses x-q=x_0a+x_1b. Project this equation to degree j. Step 1 puts π_j(q) in Q; step 2 identifies the remaining summands with x_0π_{j-1}(a) and x_1π_{j-1}(b), giving the conclusion.

theorem homogeneous_decomposition_of_quotient_span {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {N : Type v} [AddCommGroup N] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) N]
    [Module k N] [IsScalarTower k (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) N]
    (ℳ : ℤ → AddSubgroup N) (hℳ : DirectSum.IsInternal ℳ)
    (hsmul : ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : ℤ) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (x : N),
      f ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k d → x ∈ ℳ j → f • x ∈ ℳ ((d : ℤ) + j))
    (r : ℕ) (n : Fin r → N) (hn : ∀ i : Fin r, SetLike.IsHomogeneousElem ℳ (n i))
    (hgen : Submodule.span k (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦
      (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin 2 → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)) •
        (⊤ : Submodule (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) N)).mkQ (n i))) = ⊤)
    (j : ℤ) (x : N) (hx : x ∈ ℳ j) :
    ∃ q ∈ Submodule.span (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (Set.range n),
      ∃ a ∈ ℳ (j - 1), ∃ b ∈ ℳ (j - 1),
        x = q + (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) • a +
          (X 1 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) • b
